issues.failure_explanation: The signal x has length N with indices 0..N-1, but n_T = N*sum_{t in T} 1/p_t is not necessarily < N. For N = 30 (the paper's running example size) and T = {1,2,3}, n_T = 15+10+6 = 31 >= 30, so x_{n_T} is not an entry of the signal. The well-definedness argument only shows the n_T are distinct as integers, not that they lie in range nor that they are distinct modulo N. The proof as written does not define a valid length-N signal whenever sum 1/p_t >= 1 (e.g. N = 30, 60, 210,...). Since Lemma amb2D and Theorem amb2D use this signal for arbitrary lengths D, they inherit the gap.

failure_location.quote: For each subset of indices $T \subseteq \set{1, \ldots, \omega}$, define $n_T = N\sum_{t \in T} \frac{1}{p_t}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define x_{n_T mod N} and show the residues n_T mod N are distinct: n_{T_1} - n_{T_2} is N times a fraction whose lowest-terms denominator is prod_{t in T_1 Δ T_2} p_t > 1, so it is not an integer multiple of N. The DFT computation is unchanged since e^{-2πi n_T k/N} is N-periodic.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit ambiguity construction underlying the tightness/lower-bound results is ill-defined for lengths with sum of reciprocal prime factors >= 1; the lower-bound theorem and corollary rest on it.
issues.title: Construction in Lemma amb1D uses indices n_T that can exceed N-1
issues.why_classification: A short local modification (reduce indices mod N plus a two-line distinctness argument) fully restores the lemma and all dependents with no loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of the following result is identical to \Cref{lem:rep_in_time} and is omitted.

issues.failure_explanation: Computing the inverse DFT of the length-dN signal ỹ formed by stacking d copies of x̃: y_n = (1/(dN)) Σ_k x̃_k η_{dN}^{-nk} Σ_{t=0}^{d-1} η_d^{-nt}. The inner sum is d·δ_{d|n}, so y_{dn'} = (1/N) Σ_k x̃_k η_N^{-n'k} = x_{n'}, not d x_{n'}. The 1/(dN) normalization of the inverse DFT cancels the factor d, so the proof is not 'identical' to Lemma rep_in_time. Example: N=1, x=[a], d=2 gives ỹ=[a,a], y=[a,0], so y_0 = a ≠ 2a. The subsequent derivation (eq:recto1Dlambda_new, Definition subsig) is in fact consistent with y_{dn}=x_n, so only the lemma statement is wrong.

failure_location.quote:
Additionally, for all $0\le n < N$,
    $y_{dn} = dx_n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace y_{dn} = d x_n by y_{dn} = x_n and note the normalization difference from Lemma rep_in_time.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma as stated is false; downstream use only relies on the (correct) vanishing part, so no other result is invalidated.
issues.title: Lemma rep_in_freq states y_{dn} = d x_n; correct value is x_n
issues.why_classification: One-line correction of an unused conclusion; all dependents already use the correct relation.

issues.failure_explanation: gcd(k,N_1)=d_1 only guarantees gcd(k/d_1, N_1/d_1)=1, i.e. invertibility modulo D_1 = N_1/d_1, not modulo N_1. Counterexample: N_1 = 6, k = 4 gives d_1 = 2, k/d_1 = 2, and 2 has no inverse mod 6. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take (k/d_1)^{-1} modulo D_1 and (l/d_2)^{-1} modulo D_2; then m_j(k/d_1) ≡ jp (mod D_1) implies m_j k ≡ jpd_1 (mod N_1), which is all the argument uses.
issues.overall_effect: The existence half of Lemma subsig (and hence the well-definedness remark after Lemma amb2D) has a gap, though the conclusion is true.
issues.title: Lemma subsig asserts k/d_1 is invertible modulo N_1, which is false in general
issues.why_classification: Routine local fix of the modulus; the rest of the proof and all dependents survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Require a representative DFT coefficient $\tilde{X}_{k, l}$ for each coefficient class
Line~\ref{ln:2D_loop} iterates through representative frequencies $(k, l)$ of each DFT coefficient equivalence class.

issues.failure_explanation: Invert1D is called with the coefficients X̃_{λk,λl} for all divisors λ of D. For λ>1 these lie in other equivalence classes, whose supplied representative is generally not (λk,λl) itself, and knowing one coefficient of a class does not give the value of another without inverting. These values become available only after the loop has processed the class of (λk,λl) and executed the fill-in step. The algorithm prescribes no order on RepCoeffs (unlike Algorithm memo_2D, whose order is verified), so as written the call in Line 2to1 may reference undetermined data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Process representative frequencies in nondecreasing order of D (subgroup order); then all X̃_{λk,λl} for λ|D, λ>1 have been filled in by earlier iterations, since they lie in proper cyclic subgroups of ⟨(k,l)⟩ already processed.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 2D is not well defined for an arbitrary iteration order; its guarantee depends on an unstated ordering of classes.
issues.title: Algorithm 2D uses DFT coefficients not in its input and requires an unstated iteration order
issues.why_classification: Adding a one-line ordering requirement restores correctness with no loss of guarantee or complexity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \ForAll{$(k, l) \in \Call{RepCoeffs}{N_1, N_2} : \gcd(k, N_1) = N_1/D_1, \gcd(l, N_2) = N_2/D_2$} \label{ln:loop_memo2D}
Since $D_1/p < D_1$, the $(pk, pl)$-subsignal was recovered at a previous iteration of the for loop in Line~\ref{ln:outer}.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm stores x^{(k,l)} only for (k,l) in RepCoeffs, and fills X̃ only at λ coprime to D. The ILP at Line ip needs the subsignal x^{(p_j k, p_j l)}, but (p_j k, p_j l) is generally not the chosen representative of its class, so this vector is never computed or stored by any earlier iteration. The correctness argument asserts 'the (pk,pl)-subsignal was recovered' at a previous iteration, conflating the class with the specific frequency. The needed vector is recoverable (via inverse DFT of the already-filled X̃_{λpk,λpl}, or by index permutation of the representative's subsignal), but the algorithm does not specify this step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a step computing x^{(p_j k,p_j l)} as the inverse DFT of (X̃_{λ p_j k, λ p_j l})_{0≤λ<D/p_j}, all of which are filled by earlier iterations under the stated order, or as the permutation x^{(p_jk,p_jl)}_j = x^{(k'',l'')}_{μ^{-1} j mod D/p_j} where (p_jk,p_jl)=μ(k'',l'').
issues.overall_effect: As written, the ILP right-hand sides in Algorithm memo_2D are undefined for non-representative frequencies (p_j k, p_j l); the correctness argument has a corresponding gap.
issues.title: Algorithm memo_2D references subsignals x^{(p_j k, p_j l)} that it never computes
issues.why_classification: A short explicit conversion step (already implicit in the paper's FFT discussion) fixes the omission; guarantees and complexity are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
If $p \ndivs N_1$, then $\gcd(pk, N_1) = \gcd(k, N_1)$.
Additionally, $p$ must divide $N_2$

issues.failure_explanation: gcd(pk,N_1) = p·gcd(k,N_1) holds only when p divides D_1 = N_1/gcd(k,N_1). If p | N_1 but p ∤ D_1 (e.g. N_1 = 6, k = 3, D_1 = 2, p = 3 with 3 | D_2), then gcd(pk,N_1) = gcd(k,N_1) and the (pk,pl)-subsignal is recovered in the same outer iteration (earlier inner iteration), not a previous outer iteration as the argument claims. The case analysis as written does not cover this situation, so the verification of the dynamic-programming order is incomplete.

failure_location.quote: If $p \divs N_1$, then $\gcd(pk, N_1) = p\gcd(k, N_1) = N_1/(D_1/p)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split on p | D_1 versus p ∤ D_1 (in which case p | D_2 since p | D = lcm(D_1,D_2)); the two conclusions then follow exactly as written.
issues.overall_effect: The correctness argument for the iteration order of Algorithm memo_2D has an uncovered case; the algorithm's ordering is nonetheless valid.
issues.title: Case split in memo_2D ordering proof uses p | N_1 instead of p | D_1
issues.why_classification: Replacing the case condition is a routine local repair that preserves the algorithm and its guarantee.

With the tabulated count, the 11×13 matrices used a larger fraction of their spectrum than the 60×60 matrices (9.7%), so the stated conclusion that the 11×13 case was inverted from a relatively smaller sampled spectrum is not supported by the paper's own data.
